 GAME DAY: Preds at Bruins, October 22
 Nashville Visits Boston to Begin Two-Game Trip
 By 
 Brooks Bratten 
 @brooksbratten 
 Senior Content Manager & Beat Reporter 
 October 22, 2026 
 Link copied 
 Nashville Predators (3-2-3, 9 pts.) vs. Boston Bruins (7-2-1, 15 pts.) 
 6 p.m. CT | TD Garden
 Watch: Scripps Sports/The Spot - Nashville 28 ; PredsTV App (in-market); ESPN+ (out-of-market)
 Listen: 102.5 The Game, Preds Radio Network
 Live Stats: GameCenter 
 ...
 The Nashville Predators begin a two-game trip tonight when they face the Boston Bruins for a 6 p.m. CT puck drop at TD Garden. This evening’s contest is the first of two meetings between the two clubs this season; the Preds will host the Bruins in March. 
 The Predators finished off their three-game homestand on Saturday night with a 5-2 victory over St. Louis. Since then, the group has had a pair of practices to rest and regroup as they’ll now begin a stretch of six games in 10 days, and three contests in the next four. 
 Following their spirited practice sessions this week, the Predators will now face a Bruins team that had won five straight before falling to the Stars on Tuesday night in overtime. They’re looking forward to that challenge and building off of their own win on Saturday. 
 “I think we just keep trying to stack our game a little bit, right? Grow our game, build it,” Preds Head Coach Andrew Brunette said following Wednesday’s practice. “I think we've worked on a lot of things. It was a short camp. We're ironing some of those things out, and there's stretches where you could see the progress, and there’s stretches like the first period the other night [where we were] a little bit sloppy. So, just that mentality of being ready. Obviously, it's two tough games [on this trip]. Take one at a time here in Boston, and we’ve got to make sure our start [is great].” 
 Preds forward Mavrik Bourque, who has missed the last four games with an upper-body injury, practiced in full again on Wednesday and took line rushes as well. Brunette said following the session he’s hopeful Bourque will return “soon, if it’s not [tonight in Boston].” 
 Defenseman Ilya Lyubushkin, who has yet to make his Preds debut this season, saw time paired with Brady Skjei during Wednesday's practice. 
 ​
 Mavrik Bourque (upper-body, day-to-day) taking the #Preds morning skate in Boston. Andrew Brunette said yesterday he's hopeful to have Bourque back in the lineup soon, if not tonight.
— Brooks Bratten (@brooksbratten) October 22, 2026 
 Last Time Out:  
 Five different goal scorers - Jonathan Marchessault, Filip Forsberg, Adam Edstrom, Ryan O’Reilly and Jack Drury - helped the Preds to a 5-2 victory over the Blues last Saturday night. Adam Wilsby recorded a career-high three assists, Roman Josi and Steven Stamkos each added a pair of helpers and Juuse Saros made 24 saves for his third win of the season. 
 Stamkos leads the Preds with four goals and 10 points, followed by Josi with eight helpers and nine points. O’Reilly and Edstrom have four goals apiece, and Forsberg has seven assists as well.
 Brunette speaks to the media ahead of game against Boston
 All-Time Meetings:  
 The Preds are 18-18-(1)-4 all-time against the Bruins, including a 6-9-(1)-4 mark on the road. Nashville is 4-4-2 in the last 10 meetings versus Boston and 2-3-0 in the last five at TD Garden.
 Nashville Notables:  
 The Predators power play ranks third in the NHL, operating at 29.6 percent (8-for-27). Jonathan Marchessault (2), Steven Stamkos (2), Ryan O’Reilly (2), Nils Hoglander (1) and Matthew Wood (1) have scored for Nashville with the man advantage.
 Jonathan Marchessault scored his first career NHL goal on April 11, 2015 vs. Boston (Tuukka Rask). Marchessault played in his 700th career game on March 4, 2025 against the Bruins.
 Nic Hague scored his first career NHL goal on Jan. 21, 2020 at Boston (Jaroslav Halak).
 Steven Stamkos recorded his 600th career assist in a two-assist game vs. Boston on March 5, 
 Alex Kerfoot scored his first career NHL goal on Oct. 11, 2017 vs. Boston (Tuukka Rask).

 Watch & Listen:  
 New this season, Preds fans can watch all locally broadcast Predators games on The Spot – Nashville 28 (WNPX) over the air with an antenna or on cable and satellite distributors serving the Predators territory.
 Predators fans within the team’s TV viewing area can also stream 81 locally broadcast games for just $74 – less than $1 per game.
 Nashville’s games will be streamed on the Nashville Predators App, which is available on the following devices:
 iOS/Android
 Amazon Fire TV
 Android TV
 Apple TV
 Roku
 Web via PredsTV.com
 The season pass also includes access to on-demand game replays and exclusive content, such as “Inside Smashville,” a weekly magazine show that launches Friday, Oct. 2 on The Spot – Nashville 28 and Predators streaming platforms.
 In addition to 81 of the team’s regular-season games being available on The Spot – Nashville 28 and via the Nashville Predators App stream, the remaining three contests will be exclusively broadcast on ESPN+.
